title: Integrating multi-modal remote sensing, deep learning, and attention mechanisms for yield prediction in plant breeding experiments
key_finding: An attention-based stacked-LSTM fusing UAV hyperspectral imagery, LiDAR point clouds and weather predicted plot-level maize yield in a genetics-focused trial with R2 of 0.82-0.93, and its temporal attention weights aligned with known growth stages.
wow_factor: The network learned on its own which growth stages matter, so interpretable AI agrees with plant physiology.
citation_short: Aviles Toledo C et al. (2024) Frontiers in Plant Science 15:1408047. doi:10.3389/fpls.2024.1408047
full_citation: Aviles Toledo C et al. (2024). Integrating multi-modal remote sensing, deep learning, and attention mechanisms for yield prediction in plant breeding experiments. Frontiers in Plant Science 15:1408047. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2024.1408047

title: RhizoNet segments plant roots to assess biomass and growth for enabling self-driving labs
key_finding: RhizoNet, a Residual U-Net workflow with convex-hull post-processing, segmented root biomass in thousands of EcoFAB hydroponic scans across nutrient treatments and generalised across experiments, positioned as a component of self-driving labs.
wow_factor: Root growth, the hidden half of the plant, can be tracked automatically in closed-loop autonomous experiments.
citation_short: Sordo Z et al. (2024) Scientific Reports 14:12907. doi:10.1038/s41598-024-63497-8
full_citation: Sordo Z et al. (2024). RhizoNet segments plant roots to assess biomass and growth for enabling self-driving labs. Scientific Reports 14:12907. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-63497-8

title: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting
key_finding: GraphCast, a graph neural network trained on reanalysis, forecasts hundreds of variables 10 days ahead at 0.25 degree resolution in under 1 minute and outperformed the best operational deterministic system on 90% of 1,380 verification targets.
wow_factor: A 10-day global forecast that took supercomputer hours now runs in under a minute.
citation_short: Lam R et al. (2023) Science 382:1416-1421. doi:10.1126/science.adi2336
full_citation: Lam R et al. (2023). Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting. Science 382:1416-1421. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adi2336

title: Probabilistic weather forecasting with machine learning
key_finding: GenCast, a diffusion-based ensemble model, produces 15-day global forecasts for over 80 variables at 0.25 degrees in 8 minutes and beat ECMWF's ENS ensemble on 97.2% of 1,320 targets, including extremes.
wow_factor: Probabilistic AI ensembles give breeders and agronomists risk distributions rather than a single forecast.
full_citation: Price I et al. (2025). Probabilistic weather forecasting with machine learning. Nature 637:84-90 (online 4 Dec 2024). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08252-9

title: Neural general circulation models for weather and climate
key_finding: NeuralGCM couples a differentiable atmospheric dynamics solver with learned components, matching ML models at 1-10 days and ECMWF ensembles at 1-15 days, and tracking climate metrics for decades at orders-of-magnitude lower compute; the authors note it does not extrapolate to substantially different future climates.
wow_factor: The hybrid physics-plus-learning recipe that works for the atmosphere is the template for next-generation crop models.
full_citation: Kochkov D et al. (2024). Neural general circulation models for weather and climate. Nature 632:1060-1066. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07744-y

title: A foundation model for the Earth system
key_finding: Aurora, a foundation model trained on over a million hours of diverse geophysical data, outperformed operational forecasts for air quality, ocean waves, tropical-cyclone tracks and high-resolution weather at orders of magnitude lower compute, and can be fine-tuned to new domains cheaply.
wow_factor: Pretraining and fine-tuning, the same pattern as language models, now applies to the whole Earth system and could be fine-tuned for agro-climate variables.
full_citation: Bodnar C et al. (2025). A foundation model for the Earth system. Nature 641:1180-1187. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09005-y

title: How AI is helping 38 million farmers with advance weather predictions
venue: Google blog / UChicago Institute for Climate and Sustainable Growth
key_finding: In 2025, a blend of NeuralGCM, ECMWF's AIFS and historical data predicted Indian monsoon onset up to a month ahead, including an unusual mid-season dry spell, and forecasts were sent by SMS to 38 million farmers with India's Ministry of Agriculture.
wow_factor: An AI weather model went from a Nature paper to SMS messages for 38 million farmers within about a year.
citation_short: Google Research & University of Chicago (2025) Google blog / UChicago Institute for Climate and Sustainable Growth [company]. https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/research/indian-farmers-monsoon-prediction/
full_citation: Google Research & University of Chicago (2025). How AI is helping 38 million farmers with advance weather predictions. Google blog / UChicago Institute for Climate and Sustainable Growth. https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/research/indian-farmers-monsoon-prediction/

title: Decision-oriented benchmarking to transform AI weather forecast access: Application to the Indian monsoon
key_finding: A benchmarking framework linking meteorology, AI and social science showed that AI weather models skilfully predict an agriculturally relevant local monsoon-onset index weeks ahead out-of-sample, and it informed model selection for the 2025 forecasts sent to 38 million farmers.
wow_factor: Models are evaluated on whether they improve a farmer's sowing decision, not only on global error scores.
citation_short: Masiwal R et al. (2026) arXiv preprint [preprint]. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2602.03767
full_citation: Masiwal R et al. (2026). Decision-oriented benchmarking to transform AI weather forecast access: Application to the Indian monsoon. arXiv preprint. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2602.03767

title: Integrating data assimilation, crop model, and machine learning for winter wheat yield forecasting in the North China Plain
key_finding: Assimilating LAI and soil moisture into a crop model, adding weather forecasts, then stacking ML raised North China Plain winter-wheat yield forecasts from ACC 0.69 / MAPE 7.79% (1-3 months ahead) to ACC 0.97 / MAPE 1.74%.
wow_factor: Stacking ML on a data-assimilated crop model cut forecast MAPE from 7.79% to 1.74%, about a 4.5-fold reduction.
citation_short: Zhuang H et al. (2024) Agricultural and Forest Meteorology 347:109909. doi:10.1016/j.agrformet.2024.109909
full_citation: Zhuang H et al. (2024). Integrating data assimilation, crop model, and machine learning for winter wheat yield forecasting in the North China Plain. Agricultural and Forest Meteorology 347:109909. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.agrformet.2024.109909

title: NeuralCrop: Combining physics and machine learning for improved crop yield projections
key_finding: NeuralCrop, a differentiable hybrid global gridded crop model first trained to emulate a process-based model and then fine-tuned on observations, matched state-of-the-art models, reproduced yield anomalies better especially under drought, and ran orders of magnitude faster.
wow_factor: This is the NeuralGCM approach applied to crops: a differentiable crop model that learns from data and still respects physiology.
citation_short: Lin Y et al. (2025) arXiv preprint [preprint]. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2512.20177
full_citation: Lin Y et al. (2025). NeuralCrop: Combining physics and machine learning for improved crop yield projections. arXiv preprint. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2512.20177

title: An agricultural digital twin for mandarins demonstrates the potential for individualized agriculture
key_finding: An Open-API digital twin for mandarins on Jeju Island (~185,000 ha) integrated regional, inter-orchard and intra-orchard data; intra-orchard variation explained fruit quality substantially more than inter-orchard variation.
wow_factor: Digital twins point toward individualized agriculture, in which each tree is managed like a patient in personalised medicine.
citation_short: Kim S & Heo S (2024) Nature Communications 15:1561. doi:10.1038/s41467-024-45725-x
full_citation: Kim S & Heo S (2024). An agricultural digital twin for mandarins demonstrates the potential for individualized agriculture. Nature Communications 15:1561. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-45725-x

title: Data-driven crop growth simulation on time-varying generated images using multi-conditional generative adversarial networks
key_finding: A multi-conditional Wasserstein GAN generated realistic future images of Arabidopsis, cauliflower and faba bean-wheat mixtures from an early image, growth time and treatment; adding process-based simulated biomass as a condition improved traits derived from generated images.
wow_factor: Generative AI can show what a plot will look like weeks ahead under a different cultivar or sowing density.
citation_short: Drees L et al. (2024) Plant Methods 20:93. doi:10.1186/s13007-024-01205-3
full_citation: Drees L et al. (2024). Data-driven crop growth simulation on time-varying generated images using multi-conditional generative adversarial networks. Plant Methods 20:93. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13007-024-01205-3

title: LSTM-attention-guided graph neural networks for integrated genotype–Environment modeling in maize yield prediction
key_finding: Encoding weather with an LSTM and 437,214 SNPs as genotype nodes in an attention GNN, the best architecture predicted 2022 maize yield for unseen genotypes and environments with RMSE 2.212 and r = 0.695, reducing RMSE about 20% compared with the base graph and beating the G x E competition winner.
wow_factor: Graph neural networks place genotypes and environments in one network and predict new hybrids in new environments.
verified_via: crossref abstract (Crossref 'new version' update, not a retraction)
citation_short: Morshedian A & Domaratzki M (2026) PLOS Computational Biology 22:e1013729. doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1013729
full_citation: Morshedian A & Domaratzki M (2026). LSTM-attention-guided graph neural networks for integrated genotype–Environment modeling in maize yield prediction. PLOS Computational Biology 22:e1013729. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1013729

title: Structured Multimodal Deep Learning improves Genomic Prediction in Future Environments
key_finding: The Structured Interaction Neural Network separates genetic, environmental and interaction effects and reached accuracy 0.63 for next-cycle maize yield against 0.43 for BLUP and 0.48 for a prior neural net, and lowered benchmark RMSE to 2.41 vs 2.46 Mg/ha.
wow_factor: Deep learning beat BLUP once statistical-genetics structure was built in, which counters the common view that DL does not help genomic prediction.
citation_short: Potze A et al. (2025) bioRxiv preprint [preprint]. doi:10.1101/2025.09.05.674546
full_citation: Potze A et al. (2025). Structured Multimodal Deep Learning improves Genomic Prediction in Future Environments. bioRxiv preprint. https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.09.05.674546

title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist (v1 title: Towards an AI co-scientist)
key_finding: Google's Gemini-based multi-agent system generates, critiques and refines hypotheses through a tournament-style evolution; automated evaluations show hypothesis quality keeps improving with more test-time compute, and drug-repurposing candidates for acute myeloid leukemia were validated in vitro.
wow_factor: A team of AI agents that debate each other's ideas produced hypotheses that survived real wet-lab tests.
citation_short: Gottweis J et al. (2025) arXiv [preprint]. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2502.18864
full_citation: Gottweis J et al. (2025). Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist (v1 title: Towards an AI co-scientist). arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2502.18864

title: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
key_finding: Robin combines literature-search and data-analysis agents to run the hypothesis–experiment–analysis loop; it proposed and validated ripasudil, a clinically used ROCK inhibitor never previously proposed for dry age-related macular degeneration, and then designed and analysed a follow-up RNA-seq experiment.
wow_factor: An AI system went from literature to a validated drug-repurposing candidate, then designed its own follow-up experiment.
citation_short: Ghareeb AE et al. (2026) Nature. doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10652-y
full_citation: Ghareeb AE et al. (2026). A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery. Nature. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10652-y

title: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
key_finding: The AI Scientist generates ideas, writes code, runs experiments, writes the manuscript and reviews it; one fully AI-generated manuscript passed first-round peer review at a top-tier ML-conference workshop with a 70% acceptance rate.
wow_factor: A machine-written paper passed human peer review, and the system's design is now itself a peer-reviewed Nature paper.
full_citation: Lu C et al. (2026). Towards end-to-end automation of AI research. Nature. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10265-5

title: Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist: Bold Claims, Mixed Results, and a Promising Future?
key_finding: An independent evaluation found that 42% of the AI Scientist's experiments failed because of coding errors, novelty checks misclassified established ideas as new, and manuscripts had a median of five citations (only 5 of 34 from 2020 or later).
wow_factor: Students can see how independent testing pushes back on bold claims about AI scientists.
citation_short: Beel J et al. (2025) arXiv [preprint]. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2502.14297
full_citation: Beel J et al. (2025). Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist: Bold Claims, Mixed Results, and a Promising Future?. arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2502.14297

title: Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery
key_finding: Kosmos runs for up to 12 hours over 200 agent rollouts, executing on average 42,000 lines of code and reading 1,500 papers per run; independent scientists judged 79.4% of report statements accurate, and collaborators said one 20-cycle run matched about 6 months of their own research.
wow_factor: One overnight run did roughly six months of a researcher's analysis, and every claim is linked to code or a paper.
citation_short: Mitchener L et al. (2025) arXiv [preprint]. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2511.02824
full_citation: Mitchener L et al. (2025). Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery. arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2511.02824

title: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
key_finding: Biomni builds its action space by mining tools, databases and protocols from tens of thousands of publications across 25 biomedical domains, then combines LLM reasoning, retrieval-augmented planning and code execution; it generalises to tasks such as causal gene prioritisation, microbiome analysis and molecular cloning without task-specific prompt tuning.
wow_factor: An agent that learned its own toolkit by reading the literature points toward a 'Biomni for crops'.
citation_short: Huang K et al. (2025) bioRxiv [preprint]. doi:10.1101/2025.05.30.656746
full_citation: Huang K et al. (2025). Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent. bioRxiv. https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.05.30.656746

title: CRISPR-GPT for agentic automation of gene-editing experiments
key_finding: The CRISPR-GPT agent helps choose CRISPR systems, design guide RNAs, plan delivery, draft protocols and analyse data; it was used to knock out four genes with Cas12a and to epigenetically activate two genes with dCas9 in human cell lines.
wow_factor: Plant gene-editing design (guides, delivery, assays) could be assisted by the same kind of agent.
citation_short: Qu Y et al. (2025) Nature Biomedical Engineering. doi:10.1038/s41551-025-01463-z
full_citation: Qu Y et al. (2025). CRISPR-GPT for agentic automation of gene-editing experiments. Nature Biomedical Engineering. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41551-025-01463-z

title: Autonomous chemical research with large language models
key_finding: Coscientist, driven by GPT-4 and given tools for web and documentation search, code execution and lab automation, designed, planned and ran experiments across six tasks, including successful optimisation of palladium-catalysed cross-coupling reactions.
wow_factor: The first LLM to operate real lab hardware on its own, the starting point for self-driving labs.
full_citation: Boiko DA et al. (2023). Autonomous chemical research with large language models. Nature. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06792-0

title: An AI Agent for Fully Automated Multi-Omic Analyses
key_finding: AutoBA is an LLM agent that plans and executes end-to-end multi-omic analyses from minimal input; it supports online or local LLM backends for data privacy and uses automated code repair to make runs more stable.
wow_factor: This is a direct ancestor of what students already do with Claude Code: describe the analysis and let the agent write, run and fix the code.
citation_short: Zhou J et al. (2024) Advanced Science. doi:10.1002/advs.202407094
full_citation: Zhou J et al. (2024). An AI Agent for Fully Automated Multi-Omic Analyses. Advanced Science. https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202407094

title: Early science acceleration experiments with GPT-5
key_finding: Case studies across mathematics, physics, astronomy, computer science, biology and materials science record where GPT-5 contributed concrete research steps and where it fell short; the collection includes four new mathematical results that the human authors checked.
wow_factor: Frontier-lab models are now documented as contributing to research, with both their successes and their failures reported openly.
citation_short: Bubeck S et al. (2025) arXiv [preprint]. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2511.16072
full_citation: Bubeck S et al. (2025). Early science acceleration experiments with GPT-5. arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2511.16072

title: AlphaEarth Foundations: An embedding field model for accurate and efficient global mapping from sparse label data
key_finding: AlphaEarth Foundations assimilates multi-source Earth-observation data into a general embedding field; its embeddings were the only ones to consistently outperform the other featurisation approaches tested across mapping evaluations without retraining, and annual global layers for 2017–2024 have been released.
wow_factor: A 'virtual satellite' for every field on Earth could become a free environmental covariate for multi-environment trials (G×E).
verified_via: arXiv API record (posted 2025-07-29); public launch reported 2025-07-30/31
citation_short: Brown CF et al. (2025) arXiv / Google DeepMind [preprint]. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2507.22291
full_citation: Brown CF et al. (2025). AlphaEarth Foundations: An embedding field model for accurate and efficient global mapping from sparse label data. arXiv / Google DeepMind. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2507.22291

title: Large language models in plant biology
key_finding: The review describes how LLM architectures extend beyond human language to DNA, protein and gene-expression sequences, and notes that the plant community had not yet widely adopted these models.
wow_factor: In 2024 the field was described as largely untouched by LLMs, which leaves open ground for this generation of students.
citation_short: Lam HYI et al. (2024) Trends in Plant Science. doi:10.1016/j.tplants.2024.04.013
full_citation: Lam HYI et al. (2024). Large language models in plant biology. Trends in Plant Science. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tplants.2024.04.013

title: From text to traits: exploring the role of large language models in plant breeding
key_finding: The review argues that LLMs could help identify genetic interactions, improve trait prediction and integrate multi-omic, phenotypic and environmental data, and states that their adoption in plant breeding was still largely unexplored.
wow_factor: A breeding-specific roadmap that lists open problems a student thesis could take on.
citation_short: Yoosefzadeh-Najafabadi M (2025) Frontiers in Plant Science. doi:10.3389/fpls.2025.1583344
full_citation: Yoosefzadeh-Najafabadi M (2025). From text to traits: exploring the role of large language models in plant breeding. Frontiers in Plant Science. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2025.1583344

title: PLLaMa: An Open-source Large Language Model for Plant Science
key_finding: PLLaMa extends LLaMa-2 with more than 1.5 million plant-science articles and is checked by an international panel that includes plant breeders; model checkpoints and code are open.
wow_factor: An open plant-science LLM trained on 1.5 million papers that anyone can download and fine-tune.
citation_short: Yang X et al. (2024) arXiv [preprint]. doi:10.48550/arxiv.2401.01600
full_citation: Yang X et al. (2024). PLLaMa: An Open-source Large Language Model for Plant Science. arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2401.01600

title: PlantGPT: An Arabidopsis-Based Intelligent Agent that Answers Questions about Plant Functional Genomics
key_finding: PlantGPT combines retrieval over more than 60,000 plant-research abstracts with Llama3-8B fine-tuned on 13,993 Arabidopsis phenotypes and 23,323 gene functions, and outperforms general LLMs on specialised gene–phenotype questions.
wow_factor: A small 8-billion-parameter model beats general chatbots on plant gene questions, so domain grounding matters more than model size here.
citation_short: Zhang R et al. (2025) Advanced Science. doi:10.1002/advs.202503926
full_citation: Zhang R et al. (2025). PlantGPT: An Arabidopsis-Based Intelligent Agent that Answers Questions about Plant Functional Genomics. Advanced Science. https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.202503926

title: PlantScience.ai: An LLM-powered virtual scientist for plant science
key_finding: PlantScience.ai builds a scientific knowledge graph automatically from the plant literature, updates it continuously and grounds each answer in cited primary sources, which targets the terminology errors and missing source traceability of general LLMs.
wow_factor: A citation-aware 'virtual plant scientist' that keeps reading new papers so researchers do not have to read all of them.
citation_short: Yu H et al. (2026) Molecular Plant. doi:10.1016/j.molp.2026.03.010
full_citation: Yu H et al. (2026). PlantScience.ai: An LLM-powered virtual scientist for plant science. Molecular Plant. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.molp.2026.03.010

title: SeedBench: A Multi-task Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Seed Science
key_finding: SeedBench, built with domain experts to simulate steps of modern seed breeding, was used to evaluate 26 proprietary, open-source and domain-fine-tuned LLMs and found substantial gaps between LLM capability and real seed-science problems.
wow_factor: The first benchmark built around breeding tasks shows that current LLMs are still far from expert breeders.
citation_short: Ying J et al. (2025) Proceedings of ACL 2025 (Long Papers). doi:10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.1516
full_citation: Ying J et al. (2025). SeedBench: A Multi-task Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Seed Science. Proceedings of ACL 2025 (Long Papers). https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2025.acl-long.1516

title: Knowledge-guided Bayesian optimization using pre-trained LLMs speeds up the identification of superior genotypes from germplasm collection
key_finding: In a rice germplasm panel, zero-shot LLM warm-starting from passport data (name, origin, subpopulation) reduced the number of genotypes evaluated before finding the best one for seed number per panicle, with small gains for protein content; Gaussian-process Bayesian optimisation remained strongest when genomic data were available.
wow_factor: An LLM's prior knowledge of cultivar names and origins helps choose which genebank accessions to grow first.
citation_short: Hamazaki K, Tsuda K (2026) bioRxiv [preprint]. doi:10.64898/2026.06.28.735149
full_citation: Hamazaki K, Tsuda K (2026). Knowledge-guided Bayesian optimization using pre-trained LLMs speeds up the identification of superior genotypes from germplasm collection. bioRxiv. https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.06.28.735149

title: Fabrication and errors in the bibliographic citations generated by ChatGPT
key_finding: Across 636 citations in 84 ChatGPT-written literature reviews, 55% of GPT-3.5 citations and 18% of GPT-4 citations were fabricated, and 43% and 24% of the real citations, respectively, contained substantive errors.
wow_factor: The error rate dropped sharply between model generations but did not reach zero, which is why every reference in this course is checked against its DOI.
citation_short: Walters WH, Wilder EI (2023) Scientific Reports. doi:10.1038/s41598-023-41032-5
full_citation: Walters WH, Wilder EI (2023). Fabrication and errors in the bibliographic citations generated by ChatGPT. Scientific Reports. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-41032-5

title: Toward autonomous science with agentic artificial intelligence
key_finding: The perspective traces the path from prediction tools (e.g., AlphaFold) to agentic systems (Co-Scientist, Robin, Biomni) and agentic workbenches, and argues that their potential cannot be separated from hallucination, bias, irreproducibility and dual-use risks.
wow_factor: Cell frames agentic AI as a new phase of science and asks for responsible human–AI collaboration.
citation_short: Guo LY et al. (2026) Cell. doi:10.1016/j.cell.2026.08.052
full_citation: Guo LY et al. (2026). Toward autonomous science with agentic artificial intelligence. Cell. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2026.08.052

title: Bayer pilots unique generative AI tool for agriculture
key_finding: On 14 March 2024 Bayer announced the pilot of an expert GenAI system trained on years of internal data and insights from thousands of trials in its testing network, intended to support agronomists and farmers.
wow_factor: A major seed company turned decades of trial data into an assistant that answers questions in plain language.

title: Bayer's E.L.Y. Wins 'AI-based AgTech Solution of the Year' in 2025 AgTech Breakthrough Awards Program
key_finding: According to Bayer's internal benchmarks, E.L.Y. improves response times to customer questions by 60%, and employees report saving up to four hours per week; the system uses a frontier LLM with retrieval-augmented generation over agronomic data, field-trial results and label guidance.
wow_factor: A domain GenAI system already reports measurable productivity gains for agronomists in the field.

title: Anthropic launches Claude Life Sciences to give researchers an AI efficiency boost
key_finding: On 20 October 2025 Anthropic launched Claude for Life Sciences, its first formal entry into the sector, with connectors to scientific tools including Benchling, PubMed and 10x Genomics, aimed at work from literature review and hypothesis generation to data analysis and regulatory drafting.
wow_factor: The coding agent students already use is being connected to lab notebooks, literature databases and single-cell platforms.
